item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-99d96e86c8b3085c","start_unit":5,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Mexico was a signatory to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons from 20 September 2017 and ratified it on 16 January 2018; the treaty was in force during 2023.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly applicable to 2023 treaty status; the underlying decisions predate the period.","ruler_attribution":"Mexico's treaty position was established during López Obrador's presidency.","limitations":["The source establishes treaty status, not implementation, funding, or enforcement measures during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fb7886a28c029e1e","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"CIVICUS reported that Mexican authorities restricted civic space through proposed limits on foreign funding for civil-society organizations, removed tax incentives for donations, and portrayed civil society as adversarial; it also reported hostile or stigmatizing presidential rhetoric toward journalists, human-rights defenders, protesters, feminists, and environmental activists.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Evidence concerns the first half of 2022 and the administration's recent conduct, providing context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the rhetoric to López Obrador and the restrictions to his government and governing party.","limitations":["The funding restriction described was proposed legislation, not an enacted law in the supplied text.","CIVICUS reports allegations and observations rather than judicial findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fb7886a28c029e1e","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"At least 11 journalists were killed in Mexico in the first five months of 2022; the journalist-protection mechanism suffered from weak coordination, insufficient funding and staffing, delays, and protection gaps, while only six of 105 federal investigations into journalist killings since 2010 had resulted in homicide convictions.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The figures primarily concern 2022 and the period since 2010, but assess institutions operating under López Obrador's administration.","ruler_attribution":"The report assesses the Mexican government's protection and investigative institutions during his administration.","limitations":["The supplied document does not provide 2023 figures or establish personal direction by López Obrador."]},{"source_id":"SRC-789faf2ef4d6488a","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL prepared evidence for Mexico's 2023 federal budget process, including indicators on poverty, economic conditions, effective access to social rights, and historically discriminated groups; it reviewed 120 federal social-development programs using budget variation, poverty and rights linkages, complementarity, results orientation, and target compliance.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns preparation of the 2023 budget and evaluation of 2022 programs.","ruler_attribution":"This was an official evaluation input available to the federal administration; the source does not show which recommendations López Obrador adopted.","limitations":["The supplied page describes the evaluation framework and materials, not final budget decisions or program outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0e5292b5fabc29ff","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Maya Train, a presidential priority project, underwent at least five route changes and its announced cost increased from roughly 120 billion pesos in 2018 to 230 billion pesos by late 2021; official explanations cited savings, construction speed, archaeological remains, cenotes, mobility concerns, and land-acquisition costs. Planned stations changed from 17 to 21 plus 14 stops, and the Army was later designated to operate the train and receive its profits.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence concerns project planning and implementation through March 2022, relevant to the project during López Obrador's 2023 administration.","ruler_attribution":"The project was a stated priority of López Obrador, who inaugurated its construction and set its development objectives; Fonatur and other agencies implemented it.","limitations":["The source is a newspaper report and does not establish final 2023 cost, completion, or realized benefits.","La Jornada reported that Fonatur did not respond to requests for clarification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9c665a1de50c564d","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In an October 2023 statement, Mexico speaking for the New Agenda Coalition condemned threats to use nuclear weapons and escalating nuclear rhetoric, advocated concrete, transparent, verifiable, irreversible disarmament measures, stronger NPT accountability and reporting, risk-reduction and de-alerting information, and broader participation in the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.8","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Direct 2023 diplomatic position.","ruler_attribution":"The statement was delivered by Mexico's government during López Obrador's presidency.","limitations":["The statement records diplomatic advocacy, not domestic implementation, resource allocation, or measurable effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6dfef3f2e0c311f7","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"IMCO reported that in 2021, 41% of federal procurement spending used direct awards and another 4% used restricted invitations; more than 9.797 billion pesos went to recently created firms, 35 million to sanctioned providers, and 1.8 million to shell companies. It concluded that anti-corruption actions and results were insufficient, while noting that the index identifies risk signals rather than proven corruption cases.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The index was published in June 2022 and analyzes 2021 procurement, providing administrative context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern federal institutions under López Obrador's administration; they do not establish his personal involvement.","limitations":["IMCO expressly states that the index does not identify or adjudicate specific corruption cases.","The source does not provide 2023 procurement data."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a6b2642adddd059","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Leaked Sedena communications published in 2022 disclosed López Obrador's serious health conditions and an emergency 2 January transfer to a military hospital; he later publicly acknowledged that the reports were true. The same reporting stated that the documents indicated he ordered the operation to capture Ovidio Guzmán stopped after clashes in Culiacán that left at least eight people dead.","question_ids":["2B.3","2B.4","2B.6","2B.9","3B.9","4B.6","7B.1","7B.2","7B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Evidence concerns events and disclosures through September 2022, relevant as background to 2023 governance.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the health disclosure to leaked military records and reports an alleged presidential order concerning the Ovidio Guzmán operation.","limitations":["The article relies on leaked material and media reporting; the supplied text does not provide an independent official investigation of the alleged order.","The source concerns 2022 rather than a 2023 event."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3f04a442aa614979","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that after a tidal wave and Cold Front 8 displaced the El Bosque community in Tabasco in November 2023, 69 people left a temporary shelter after alleged mistreatment and a full day without food or water; the relocation process promised in April had stalled, leaving some families homeless or returning to an uninhabitable area. Amnesty also reported inadequate water, health, electricity, and education services and criticized continued oil-production policy amid the climate crisis.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Direct 2023 evidence, including events in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The appeal addresses López Obrador directly and evaluates the Mexican federal government's relocation, climate, and social-protection responsibilities.","limitations":["The allegations about shelter treatment are attributed to community reports received by Amnesty.","The supplied document does not establish the final federal response after publication."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b4b757fd64477469","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"López Obrador issued the decree approving Mexico's National Public Security Program 2022–2024 under his constitutional executive authority.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The decree was issued on 1 December 2022 and governed the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The decree is signed and issued by López Obrador as president.","limitations":["The supplied unit establishes the decree but not its substantive measures or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b4b757fd64477469","start_unit":24,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"The security program was framed as a multidimensional, inclusive shift in security policy incorporating liberties and human rights; it was made mandatory for federal agencies, assigned monitoring to Security, Finance, and Public Administration ministries, required oversight by the Public Administration Ministry, and required implementation through approved budgets.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","5B.6","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The program applied during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The institutional design was approved by López Obrador's decree and assigned responsibilities to his federal ministries.","limitations":["The source states formal obligations and monitoring arrangements but supplies no 2023 implementation or outcome evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-71ad7d8897f70eed","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"RSF reported that Mexico's constitution formally guarantees press freedom, but López Obrador and officials used combative, stigmatizing rhetoric toward journalists, including a weekly session naming alleged fake news; it reported threats and attacks rather than overt censorship laws, collusion between officials and organized crime, widespread journalist murders and disappearances, and insufficient reforms to reduce violence and impunity.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Direct 2023 country assessment, with historical figures since 2000 and conduct during López Obrador's four years in office.","ruler_attribution":"RSF directly attributes the rhetoric to López Obrador and assesses his government's failure to carry out needed reforms.","limitations":["The source provides broad country-level findings and does not quantify every 2023 incident.","It does not establish personal responsibility for crimes committed by non-state actors."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-394ea6d17701b621","SRC-c5b7610db975db47"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents provide uneven temporal coverage: several key sources concern 2021–2022 rather than 2023.","No source supplied direct evidence on Mexico's nuclear command-and-control, proliferation enforcement, arms transfers, or biological-risk safeguards.","No source supplied a comprehensive 2023 account of electoral administration, judicial independence, social-program outcomes, or macroeconomic policy attributable specifically to López Obrador."]}
